questions.question_text: Which one of the following is the rate­limiting step in the synthesis of dopamine?
questions.explanation: The rate­limiting step in the biosynthesis of dopamine is tyrosine hydroxylase, which converts tyrosine into L­DOPA.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following receptors is a ligand­gated cation channel?
questions.explanation: 5HT­3 is a ligand­gated cation channel, while all other 5HT receptors are G­protein coupled.

questions.question_text: The Nucleus of Meynert is a prominent site of localization for which neurotransmitter in the brain?
questions.explanation: Acetylcholine is localized to an ascending system of cholinergic neurons originating in the reticular formation and nucleus basalis of Meynert.

questions.question_text: The drug 'khat' (Catha edulis) has effects comparable to
questions.explanation: Cathinone, present in khat leaves, shares a pharmacological profile closely resembling that of amphetamine and operates through releasing catecholamines.

questions.question_text: Which of the following receptors increase adenylate cyclase to stimulate cell machinery?
questions.explanation: Beta receptors are Gs coupled, thus they increase adenylate cyclase.

questions.question_text: D1 and D2 receptors are mainly located in which of the following structures?
questions.explanation: D1 and D2 are predominant in the caudate and putamen.

questions.question_text: An enzyme involved in synthesis of acetylcholine is
questions.explanation: Choline acetyl transferase (ChAT) is responsible for the synthesis of acetylcholine.

questions.question_text: The neurochemical changes reported in Alzheimer's disease include

options.text: Increased levels of choline acetyl transferase

questions.explanation: In Alzheimer's, there are decreased levels of acetylcholinesterase and other neurotransmitters.

questions.question_text: Stimulation of nicotine receptors leads to the release of which of the following neurotransmitters?
questions.explanation: Stimulation of nicotine receptors leads to the release of dopamine.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is an incorrect pairing of the disease condition and the primary neurotransmitter that is abnormal in the diseases?
questions.explanation: Acetylcholine is more relevant than dopamine for Alzheimer's dementia.

questions.question_text: Which of the following neurotransmitters can be called catecholamines?
questions.explanation: Dopamine and noradrenaline are catecholamines, while serotonin is an indolamine.

questions.question_text: Which neurotransmitter plays an important role in the neurochemical changes seen in Huntington's disease?
questions.explanation: Reduced GABA is seen in Huntington's disease.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an ionotropic receptor?
questions.explanation: GABA­A opens chloride channel; it is an ionotropic receptor.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following acts as a fast acting excitatory neurotransmitter?
questions.explanation: Glutamate is a fast acting excitatory neurotransmitter.

questions.question_text: Which of the following substances serve as a precursor for GABA?
questions.explanation: GABA is synthesized from glutamate.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an amino acid neurotransmitter?
questions.explanation: Glycine is an important inhibitory amino acid neurotransmitter.

questions.question_text: Which of the following best fits GABA­A receptor?

options.text: Ligand dependent regulator of nuclear transcription

questions.explanation: GABA A receptors are ionotropic and mediate postsynaptic inhibition.

questions.question_text: Regarding excitatory amino acids which one of the following statements is incorrect?

options.text: Glutamate is the most abundant excitatory neurotransmitter
Ketamine is a selective agonist at NMDA receptors
Excitatory amino acid neurotransmitters are essential in learning and memory
Calcium entry in neurons is influenced by glutamate
Glutamate can be a potent neurotoxin when excessive

correct_answer.text: Ketamine is a selective agonist at NMDA receptors

correct_answers.text: Ketamine is a selective agonist at NMDA receptors

questions.explanation: Ketamine is a non-competitive antagonist at NMDA receptors.

questions.question_text: Which of the following best fits glucocorticoid receptor?

options.text: Ligand dependent regulators of nuclear transcription

correct_answer.text: Ligand dependent regulators of nuclear transcription

correct_answers.text: Ligand dependent regulators of nuclear transcription

questions.explanation: Glucocorticoids act via their binding to the intracellular GR (Glucocorticoid Receptor) which translocates to the nucleus to modulate gene expression.

questions.question_text: The principal location of noradrenergic neuronal cell bodies in the CNS is
questions.explanation: The principal location of noradrenaline is the locus coeruleus.

questions.question_text: The effects of magic mushroom are very similar to those of
questions.explanation: Magic mushrooms contain psilocin and psilocybin, substances that act similarly to LSD.

questions.question_text: The predominant CNS metabolite of noradrenaline is
questions.explanation: The CNS metabolite of noradrenaline is MHPG (3­methoxy,4­hydroxy phenyl glycol).

questions.question_text: Supraspinal analgesia related to opioid release is mediated by
questions.explanation: Supraspinal analgesia involves Mu receptors that mediate the effects of opioids.

questions.question_text: Which of the following receptors is stimulated when tobacco is smoked?
questions.explanation: Nicotine acts on nicotinic cholinergic receptors when tobacco is smoked.

questions.question_text: Which of the following type of glutamate receptors is crucial for the normal function of inhibitory interneurons?
questions.explanation: NMDA receptors are predominantly located on GABA interneurons, crucial for their function.

questions.question_text: The neural mechanism of memory formation may include changes in physical properties of neurons and synapses. One such change called LTP or Long Term Potentiation is mediated by
questions.explanation: NMDA receptor mediates long-term potentiation, which is crucial for memory acquisition and development.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a rosette shaped receptor?
questions.explanation: The NMDA receptor structure is atypical of most ligand-gated receptors, appearing as a 'rosette' shape.

questions.question_text: Glycine and d­serine both act as co­agonists at
questions.explanation: Glycine and d-serine serve as co-agonists at NMDA receptors, facilitating their activation.

questions.question_text: Which of the following regions in the brain is predominantly cholinergic?
questions.explanation: The nucleus basalis of Meynert is a major source of cholinergic neurons in the brain.

questions.question_text: Which of the following enzymes mediate several catalytic reactions involving amino acids that synthesize neurotransmitters such as dopamine, serotonin, and tryptamine?
questions.explanation: Monoamine oxidases catalyze the oxidation of monoamines, crucial in the metabolism of catecholamine neurotransmitters.

questions.question_text: Which of the following best describes D2 receptor?
questions.explanation: Dopamine D2 receptors act as presynaptic inhibitory receptors, inhibiting the release of dopamine.

questions.question_text: Which of the following are carrot­shaped eosinophilic inclusions seen in hematoxylin and eosin stains?
questions.explanation: Rosenthal fibers are distinctive eosinophilic inclusions associated with gliosis and certain diseases.

questions.question_text: The most abundant neurotransmitter in the median raphe nuclei is
questions.explanation: Serotonin is the primary neurotransmitter in the median raphe nuclei, influencing various functions.

questions.question_text: Tryptophan is the precursor of which of the following neurotransmitters?
questions.explanation: Tryptophan is converted to 5-hydroxytryptophan and then to serotonin.

questions.question_text: Which of the following neurotransmitters are not correctly matched with their precursors?
questions.explanation: Histidine is the precursor of histamine, not serotonin.

questions.question_text: Where do phospholipids get produced in a cell?
questions.explanation: Smooth ER is involved in the synthesis of phospholipids and steroid hormones.

questions.question_text: The enzyme involved in catabolism of GABA is
questions.explanation: GABA transaminase is the enzyme responsible for the breakdown metabolism of GABA.

questions.question_text: A 44­year­old woman is on antipsychotic depot injections. She develops a white discharge from her breasts. Hyperprolactinemia is noted. Which of the following dopamine pathways has a role in prolactin regulation?
questions.explanation: The tuberoinfundibular pathway regulates prolactin release, inhibiting prolactin secretion.
